decisions.reason: Adding an LED board does not necessarily alter the existing power-to-main-board connector partition, connector types, or pin policies.
The additional LED board does not change the power board's enclosure fit, dimensions, orientation, or mounting requirements.
The source does not change the placement or accessibility of the power board's battery and interboard connectors.
The new board contains eight addressable LEDs, but the source does not establish whether it replaces or relocates the existing charge-status LED chain associated with the main board.
The board-count change does not alter the stated I2C cable, speed, pull-up, or series-resistor requirements.
A same-message INTRODUCE already captures the small board, its eight-LED count, and its addressable LED type; no additional candidate-state change is required.
Adding a separate LED board leaves the sensor board's connector-fanout role unchanged.
The source does not specify any change to battery protection behavior or components; its unspecified reference to a power change cannot support propagation.
The new board does not entail any change to the battery NTC connector or thermal-monitoring behavior.
The source introduces another board but does not change the existing power-board BOM requirements; milestone and payment discussion is administrative.
The source does not clarify whether the eight-LED board uses the existing SK6812/GPIO13 interface or constitutes a separate LED chain requiring a new interface decision.
Adding an LED board does not necessarily change the switchable 5V sensor rail, its GPIO control, or its operating pattern.
